verdict: DTE grew revenue 6% to $3.7B and earned $470M — and agreed to sell its non-utility Vantage business for about $3B so it can focus on its Michigan electric and gas utilities.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Operating EPS was $2.30, excluding a mark-to-market item

kpis.label: Electric segment profit
kpis.note: The regulated Michigan electric utility — the core business

kpis.label: Vantage sale price
kpis.note: Sale of the non-utility business, expected to close in H1 2027

segments.name: Utility operations
segments.note: Selling electricity and natural gas to regulated customers in Michigan — 2.3M electric and 1.4M gas customers. Within it, the Electric segment earned $468M and the Gas segment lost $30M in this seasonally weak quarter for gas.

segments.name: Non-utility operations
segments.note: Businesses outside the regulated utilities — mainly DTE Vantage (custom energy projects for big customers, $110M of profit) and Energy Trading ($23M of profit). DTE has now agreed to sell Vantage for about $3B.

opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Keeping the grid, pipes and power plants running — crews, repairs and storm restoration.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants, poles and pipelines over their long lives — a non-cash charge that grows as DTE invests.

opex.name: Taxes other than income
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on plants and networks.

opex.name: Asset losses & impairments, net
opex.note: Small net charge on asset values this quarter, versus $50M a year ago.

otherDetail: Other expense of $240M, net: $317M of interest expense on borrowings, partly offset by $32M of interest income, $64M of other income, less $19M of other expenses.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel and purchased power (including gas bought for customers and for the non-utility businesses, $1,850M combined) is treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating expense lines mirror DTE's income statement. The quarter's tax line is a $107M benefit, so tax adds to profit in the flow. Segment revenue uses the utility / non-utility split from DTE's statements; segment profits quoted in the notes are from the 10-Q segment note.
oneTimers: Reported EPS of $2.25 includes a $15M pre-tax mark-to-market loss in Energy Trading (derivatives revalued without revaluing the contracts they hedge). Excluding it, operating EPS was $2.30.

DTE agreed to sell DTE Vantage for approximately $3B to investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management — the sale is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and is not in this quarter's profit.

takeaways.title: Vantage is being sold
takeaways.text: DTE agreed to sell its non-utility Vantage business for about $3B, sharpening its focus on the regulated utilities, where it plans about $44B of investment over the next five years — including $6.1B in 2026 alone.

takeaways.title: The electric utility does the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: The Electric segment earned $468M of the $470M total. Gas lost $30M in its seasonally quiet quarter, Vantage added $110M and Energy Trading $23M, while Corporate and Other lost $101M.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit flattered the bottom line
takeaways.text: DTE booked a $107M income tax benefit rather than a tax bill this quarter, which is why $363M of pre-tax profit became $470M of net income. Operating EPS, excluding a small mark-to-market item, was $2.30 vs the reported $2.25.

follow100Note: Per-$100 figures are rounded to cents; the chain lands within a cent of the $12.61 kept as profit.
